oblivion_1: THE FIRST DEPTH OF OBLIVION, THE SHORE OF THE FORGOTTEN, below the White Archive: a long winding shore of fine WHITE SAND that looks like finely shredded paper, floating over a bottomless sea of soft pale grey-violet mist. A few loose white pages lie half-buried in the sand. In the middle an islet joined by a narrow sandbar, with a ring of small nameless weathered gravestones. A toppled old white bookshelf half buried in the sand in two places. Small grey memorial stone tablets along the shore. A white marble staircase going up in the north-west, a white marble staircase going down into the mist in the south-east. Palette: paper white, ivory, pale warm grey, lavender-grey mist, a touch of ink black. Quiet, melancholic, clean and uncluttered.
oblivion_2: THE SECOND DEPTH OF OBLIVION, THE STITCHED WOOD: three remembered landscapes torn out of other lands, floating as islands in a bottomless sea of soft pale grey-violet mist: a green FOREST GLADE with leafy trees in the north-west, a pale DESERT of rippled sand with a few low sandstone rocks in the south-west, a SNOWFIELD of clean snow with snow-laden pines in the east. Their outer edges are torn like the edges of paper. They are joined by long flat bridges made of layered sheets of WHITE PAPER stitched together with dark thread. A white marble staircase going up in the forest (north), a white marble staircase going down in the south of the snowfield. Dreamlike, clean and calm.
oblivion_3: THE THIRD DEPTH OF OBLIVION, THE HALL OF FEAR: a cold, sunken hall of the White Archive seen from above with the roof removed: thick walls of cool blue-grey stone, ivory-white marble floors with faint streaks of black ink, a long pillared hall with cracked white pillars and four dreadful statues of horned shadow figures, a small side room to the west and one to the east, an antechamber, and in the north the THRONE ROOM with a broken black stone throne on a low dais at the end of a faded dark-red carpet; in the throne room's east corner a small alcove with a staircase going down into mist; a staircase going up in the south. Pale grey-violet mist all around the building. Palette: ivory, blue-grey stone, ink black, faded red. Cold and solemn, clean and uncluttered.
oblivion_4: THE FOURTH DEPTH OF OBLIVION, THE ENDLESS CORRIDOR: three IDENTICAL reading rooms of the White Archive in a row from west to east, seen from above with the roof removed, all three painted EXACTLY ALIKE (the same white bookshelves full of white books along the north wall, the same reading table in the middle, the same ivory marble floor), each joined to the next by a pair of identical short corridors (one north, one south); thick walls of cool blue-grey stone; a staircase going up in the west wall of the first room; a narrow hall at the far east with a staircase going down into mist at its south end. Pale grey-violet mist all around the building. Eerie repetition, clean and uncluttered.
oblivion_5: THE BOTTOM OF OBLIVION, THE HALL OF THE RING: one great ROUND floor of ivory-white marble floating in a bottomless sea of soft pale grey-violet mist. The outer edge of the round floor is ONE SMOOTH PERFECT CIRCLE: a clean, softly curved broken marble rim above the mist, with no corners and no tile steps (no outer wall). On the floor stands a low RING-SHAPED inner wall of cool blue-grey stone (a smooth circle too, not a polygon), closed all the way round except ONE gate opening in the north: there is NO opening and NO stair anywhere else in the inner wall. Inside the inner wall, a round inner floor where loose white pages lie in one vast spiral pattern turning around the centre (the bed of a sleeping dragon, but paint NO dragon). The only staircase is a small white marble staircase going up at the very south edge of the outer floor. Palette: ivory, white, pale silver, blue-grey stone, lavender mist. Vast, silent, clean and uncluttered.
